question: How do they demonstrate that this type of EEG has discriminative information about the intended articulatory movements responsible for speech?
pred_answer: Five binary phonological classification tasks with above-chance accuracy, kappa coefficients, tSNE separability, and 22.51% average improvement over baselines
raw:
They formulate it as five binary classification problems on imagined-speech EEG data—presence/absence of consonants, phonemic nasal, bilabial, high-front vowels and high-back vowels—and evaluate a subject-invariant mixed CNN-LSTM-DAE/Extreme Gradient Boost model using PHASE-ONE random train/development/test splits and PHASE-TWO leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. They report above-chance accuracies, kappa coefficients, tSNE separability, and large improvements over baselines, including a maximum above-chance accuracy of 75.92% for presence/absence of the vowel task and an average margin of 22.51% over existing methods across all five binary classification tasks.

Answer: Five binary phonological classification tasks with above-chance accuracy, kappa coefficients, tSNE separability, and 22.51% average improvement over baselines

question: How do they demonstrate that this type of EEG has discriminative information about the intended articulatory movements responsible for speech?
pred_answer: By subject-invariant classification of five binary phonological/articulatory tasks from speech-imagery EEG, supported by kappa coefficients and tSNE feature separability.
raw:
The excerpts say they demonstrate this by developing a subject-invariant mapping of EEG data to different phonological categories that vary in underlying articulator motions, and by showing that their mixed deep neural network can classify five binary phonological/articulatory tasks from speech-imagery EEG data, outperforming baseline methods. They also use kappa coefficients and tSNE visualizations to indicate discriminative information beyond random decisions and separability of learned features.

Answer: By subject-invariant classification of five binary phonological/articulatory tasks from speech-imagery EEG, supported by kappa coefficients and tSNE feature separability.

question: How does PolyResponse architecture look like?
pred_answer: A single large conversational search engine / deep neural network ranking model with shared text encoders f(context) and g(reply), a MobileNet-based photo encoder t(photo), and scaled cosine-similarity retrieval of text replies and photos.
raw:
PolyResponse is powered by a single large conversational search engine, implemented as a deep neural network ranking model.
